stories.headline: Ukraine says Russia violated Trump’s surprise ‘energy ceasefire’ amid strikes on power infrastructure

sources.body:
Liza Fokht BBC News Russian, Senior Reporter

Russia’s evasive comments on the "energy ceasefire" show just how justified Ukrainian concerns were that the US had struck a diesel deal with Russia without getting anything in return.

It is already clear that the agreement to sell diesel to the US is, first and foremost, a symbolic victory for Vladimir Putin.

The Russian president can now claim that he personally helped President Trump at an important moment, while also gaining another opportunity to deepen tensions between Kyiv and Washington.

Russia also has more to gain than the potential revenue from diesel sales. More broadly, Moscow’s war effort is constrained by US intelligence-sharing with Ukraine and by the continued flow of American weapons, even if Europe is now paying for them.

But even if Moscow’s most ambitious hopes do not materialise, the minimum objective has already been achieved: Russia is once again striking deals with the US without any Ukrainian or European involvement, receiving carrots rather than sticks – and without agreeing to any compromises on ending the war.
sources.headline: Ukraine doesn't deserve 'respite', Russian FM says, as Zelensky says he'd support Trump's energy ceasefire

sources.body:
The EU also announced that it officially added almost 1,600 new sanctions on Russia’s military industrial complex.

Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of violating the “energy ceasefire” that United States President Donald Trump unilaterally announced at the weekend and promised to respond if the attacks continue.

Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum via videolink on Monday, the Ukrainian president urged the US to step in to ensure ⁠that Moscow abided by the truce, noting that there have already been “Russian violations of the energy ceasefire announced by ‌President Trump.”

“We are waiting for the details of the conditions between the Americans and Russians, ⁠and we are waiting ⁠to see what specific steps the Americans are ready to take,” said Zelenskyy, who expressed surprise at the ceasefire deal.

“This ⁠energy ceasefire, it can work, and it can become a major step toward ending ‌the war if the Americans truly step in now and make ‌sure ‌Russians respect it … If Russia does not agree to an energy ceasefire, we will respond,” Zelenskyy told the Warsaw Security Forum.

Trump’s announcement on Sunday that the two countries had agreed to an “energy ceasefire” caused confusion. It came two days after Trump declared a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian diesel, prompting outrage from European allies and Kyiv, who said it would only embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Both Ukraine and Russia have been launching mutual attacks on each other’s energy infrastructure for months, adding to upward pressure on global energy prices that have risen amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Zelenskyy initially denied any knowledge of the agreement and said it was “news to him,” according to Axios.

Trump has previously taken to his Truth Social account to announce truces or other arrangements before either Kyiv or Moscow confirmed them.

“An energy ceasefire and other steps to reduce escalation and guarantee security are truly needed here in reality, not just on Truth Social,” Zelenskyy added.

European leaders expressed encouragement at the proposed ceasefire, but agreed with Zelenskyy that it had not taken effect.

“I have not noted, over‌ the last 48 hours, any energy ceasefire coming from the ‌Russian ‌side,” French President Emmanuel Macron told reporters at a Paris autoshow.

At the Warsaw Security Forum, ⁠Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that “Russia is not interested in ‌a ceasefire, de-escalation, or peace … that is why I will go to Brussels to urge all European partners ⁠to consider increasing ⁠sanctions.”

In Brussels, the European Union announced that it has officially added almost 1,600 new sanctions on Russia’s military industrial complex, including individuals and entities involved in its four-and-a-half-year war , in a bid to maintain pressure on Moscow.

“This is the single largest expansion of our sanctions list since Russia started its war,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas wrote online. “Europe is again showing a united front … We are making it significantly harder, slower and more expensive for Russia to produce the weapons it uses to kill Ukrainians,” she added.
sources.headline: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy accuses Russia of violating Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’

stories.headline: Houthi attacks hit Riyadh airport again as Saudi Arabia suspends more flights

sources.body:
Saudi Arabia's energy minister has vowed a "serious" response to the deadly attacks on the kingdom's airports and oil and gas facilities by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement.

"The events of recent weeks are serious. Our response must be equally serious," Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman told the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh.

On Sunday, a Pakistani man was killed in an attack on a terminal at the capital's King Khalid International Airport, Saudi authorities said. It came a day after a Houthi missile hit another terminal, killing 13 people and forcing its closure.

The Houthis said they launched the attacks in retaliation for "brutal Saudi aggression" against areas they control in western Yemen.

The Houthi-run health ministry said a child was killed and six other people were injured in a Saudi air strike on a home in the capital, Sanaa, on Sunday.

A Saudi-led coalition has been providing air support for Yemeni pro-government forces battling the Houthis on Yemen's Red Sea coast and other areas.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they say is a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. The Yemeni government claimed it was behind that strike, saying it was trying to prevent an unauthorised Iranian plane from landing.

Last month, the Houthis launched a surprise offensive along Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and ousted pro-government forces from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the southern end of the Red Sea.

They said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.

However, the seizure of the strait contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports after the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

Last week, the Yemeni government announced the start of a new offensive aimed at retaking all territory held by the Houthis.

Pro-government forces said they were quickly able to retake areas around Bab al-Mandab with the help of intense Saudi air strikes, but the Houthis denied losing any territory.
sources.headline: Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports

sources.body:
Energy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breaches stretched defences

Saudi Arabia was forced to extend the suspension of all flights to and from its main international airport in Riyadh on Monday after a further round of Houthi missile attacks caused more damage and left one dead.

The Gulf nation said it was taking the step after Houthi missiles killed 13 people on Saturday and left more than 300 injured. Saudi state TV broadcast CCTV footage that showed passengers deluged in smoke and falling masonry as they queued at the airport terminal to board a plane just as the Houthi missile struck.

King Khalid international airport was being kept closed to complete verification of the airport’s safety, the Saudi aviation authority said. Saudi Arabia’s military spokesperson also said further missile and drone threats had been detected.

The closure came as the country pressed ahead with the 25th WPC Energy Conference in Riyadh, hoping to project an image of normality.

The Saudi energy minister, Abdulaziz bin Salman, told the conference that “fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon”, emphasising that the resilience of the kingdom’s energy system and the determination of its people to confront crises.

An urgent review is under way as to how Houthi missiles are repeatedly penetrating badly stretched Saudi air defences. Schoolchildren and some office workers were advised to work from home. The Houthis have also targeted the city of Khamis Mushait, and the King Fahd international airport in Dammam.

Interceptor missiles are needed to protect government buildings, oil facilities and infrastructure hubs across a wide geographic area. The Houthis have vowed to attack Saudi airports across the country.

Houthi attacks since last month have targeted fuel tanks at Riyadh airport and its affiliated warehouses, destroying a parked Airbus A320 passenger plane and damaging at least five other aircraft.

The crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, has not been seen in public since Tuesday last week, reflecting the pressure he is under to find a way out from a war that has intermittently dogged his leadership since 2014.

Inside Yemen , fighting continued in and around Taiz, the third city, and the most populous governorate, with Saudi air planes mounting eight separate strikes on any assembly of Houthi forces. As many as 60 fighters died on Sunday from both sides.

The governor of Taiz, Nabil Shamsan, on Sunday issued an urgent call to lift the Houthi siege and warned a shortage of medicines meant the city would soon run out of emergency surgical and intensive care services.

Overall the Houthis claimed the Saudis had mounted 124 raids through Sunday. The Saudis are seeking to locate Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, the reclusive leader of the Houthis, with rumours of his assassination repeatedly circulating, but Saudi Arabia does not seem to have contemporary intelligence on his precise whereabouts either in the capital Sana’a or in its stronghold of Saada.
sources.headline: Saudi Arabia further suspends flights after latest deadly Houthi attack on airport

sources.body: A new attack hit Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, a day after another attack on the airport killed at least 12 people and injured over 300. This was the deadliest on Saudi soil in over a decade. Fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have been escalating for several weeks. Story by Juliette Brown and Caitlin Brown.
sources.headline: Saudi Arabia: Riyadh airport struck again by Yemen's Houthis

stories.headline: Iran urges Saudi Arabia to pursue diplomacy as Yemen conflict escalates

sources.body:
Tehran offers to facilitate talks between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis following deadly strikes on the kingdom.

Iran has urged rival Saudi Arabia to pursue a diplomatic solution to its escalating conflict with the Houthi armed group in Yemen, warning that continued military action would only worsen the situation.

“Insisting on a military approach and disregarding a political solution would only further complicate the situation,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Saudi Arabian Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan during a telephone call on Sunday, according to a statement from Tehran.

The Saudi state news agency reported that the two ministers discussed the recent escalation in violence in the region after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), launched deadly air attacks on Saudi airports.

In a post on Telegram on Sunday, Araghchi emphasised that insisting on a military approach while disregarding political solutions would further complicate the situation. The Iranian minister said the region’s crises have no military solutions.

Araghchi said Iran is ready to provide any assistance necessary to facilitate the start of dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen and to help achieve a political solution.

In a media briefing on Monday, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaiel Baghaei also stressed that Tehran was open to resolving the conflict through dialogue.

“We do not want hostilities to continue between two Muslim countries, especially as the region is already facing tensions caused by the United States and Israel” Baghaei said.

“We have consistently stressed that the people of Yemen have the right to live with dignity, free from pressure, sanctions and blockade” Baghaei added, emphasising Iran’s “readiness to help resolve the issue through dialogue.”

Military defence and maritime analyst Alexandru Hudisteanu told Al Jazeera that Iran’s offer to mediate talks to end strikes on Saudi Arabia adds to evidence that Houthi attacks on the Kingdom are coordinated with Tehran.

“I think that while a week ago, we were wondering whether there is any strict coordination between the Houthis’ action in Saudi Arabia with Iran, especially in the maritime aspects with an uptick of attacks on shipping, right now, it is hard to think that that coordination does not exist,” Hudisteanu said.

“There is a high probability that Iran is behind these particular set of attacks,” Hudisteanu said, adding that the attacks on Saudi Arabia were a “core reflection of how Iran sees the region, where Iran wants to be a power broker and will instrument its proxies.”

Following an attack on the Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 others on Saturday, US President Donald Trump said he would reconsider the role of the United States in Yemen, adding that he was also weighing resuming strikes on Iran.

The remarks represent a departure from the president’s comments on Thursday that Washington will not resume strikes on Iran until after the US midterm elections early next month.
sources.headline: Iran urges Saudi Arabia to pursue diplomacy after Houthis escalate attacks

stories.headline: EU moves to cap Chinese hybrid-vehicle imports at 350,000 annually

sources.body:
Brussels uses WTO rules to quickly impose quota, which will halve Chinese market share to 3%

VW boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic industry

The EU is to limit the number of hybrid electric vehicles imported from China to 350,000 cars a year, the European Commission has confirmed.

Imports have been soaring in the past two years; about 800,000 battery and plug-in hybrids are likely to be sold this year.

The EU expects that the quota, which will come into force in December, will halve China’s market share, which now stands at 6% in a landmark four-year agreement made in Beijing last week .

The annual limit on imports of hybrids will be taken under the World Trade Organization safeguard measures, which mean it can be implemented swiftly without the type of investigations needed in anti-dumping measures.

Any cars imported above the quota level will not be subject to tariffs, but will remain blocked in customs at docks in Europe.

Chinese vehicles assembled within the EU, such as those made in Hungary or, in future, Spain, will not be subject to the quota, officials have confirmed, but EU companies making cars in China will.

China’s exports of hybrids to the EU tripled to €6.7bn (£5.7bn) in the first half of this year, from €2.2bn a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data.

As part of the deal, China has also agreed to drop some tariffs on auto parts and cut duties by half on footwear, olive oil and ice-cream from the EU.

Officials stressed that the quota is fully supported by China, and further dialogue on cars and other imports including chemicals, renewable energy and furniture is continuing.

“We will continue the dialogue on some products … this is by no means the end of the story,” an official said.

Last month, the EU called for feedback on a new rule that could oblige companies to diversify their supply chains while the “Made in Europe” legislation would do the same in public procurement.

On Thursday, EU leaders will discuss a French-German proposal for a “kill switch” or new instrument that would allow Brussels to block access to the single market for certain goods in the event of any harmful development, such as a ban on rare earths crucial for the tech and automotive industries.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning

The deal on hybrid EVs comes amid mounting concern over the £1bn-a-day trade deficit the EU is now running with China.

Up until recently, the EU’s strategy for tackling what it says is an “unsustainable” trade imbalance has been to seek to increase exports to China.

Sources said there has been “a paradigm shift” with concerns of deindustrialisation and job losses in the industrial heartlands forcing a renewed focus on curbing imports rather than increasing exports.

“We are closely surveilling, our imports. We know what’s coming in. We know where there’s a surge, and we know what hits the hardest in terms of our deindustrialisation,” said an official.

Andrew Small, the director of the Asia programme at the European Council for Foreign Relations, said China was likely to “suck the EU into drawn-out negotiations” on other sectors but the mood had changed in the EU.
sources.headline: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year

sources.body: The Paris Motor Show opens its doors today, and with it come mounting economic and diplomatic issues. The European Union has just announced that it has secured a commitment from China to moderate the flow of hybrid vehicles into the block's market. It opens the prospect of cutting China's export by more than a half and could prevent millions of Chinese cars from being shipped to Europe. Are European automakers capable of withstanding this competition and their dependence on China? This report from France 2 and Morgan Ayre.
sources.headline: Are European automakers capable of withstanding Chinese competition?

stories.headline: Trump faces backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia

sources.body:
US President Donald Trump is facing a growing backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia as the Iran war continues to impact global energy prices.

Trump on Friday announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately "to the American and global marketplace" followed by several other shipments.

That is despite signing legislation to authorise fresh US sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas just weeks ago.

The move has been criticised by some Republican and Democratic lawmakers, who believe the deal violates US laws.

As well as the initial release of 300,000 tonnes of diesel, Trump said Russia would then supply 500,000 tonnes in November and one million more after that.

This would be followed by a further three million tonnes, which would be delivered "within a short period" dependent on the condition of its refineries, which have been attacked by Ukraine during the ongoing war between the two countries.

"Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak confirmed these numbers to Tass, the country's state-owned news agency, saying the export volume could reach three million tonnes per month in future.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called the deal a gift to Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended".

It is understood the US Treasury is suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April as part of the deal, but other assets like those in American banks are still frozen.

A group of seven senators - four Republicans and three Democrats – on Sunday said the deal violated US laws, urging Trump to "reverse course".

"The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians," the lawmakers said.

They added that Congress had "explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin's brutal war against Ukraine".

The statement was signed by Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, Thom Tillis and John Curtis, as well as Democrats Jeanne Shaheen, Richard Blumenthal and Ron Wyden.

Not everyone is opposed to the deal. Republican Thomas Massie, who has sparred with Trump a number of issues, said the US should lift sanctions on all petroleum products.

Trump's Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News the agreement would work through existing legal channels the US has to help bring prices down and that anyone in Congress who said it would not was wrong.

Global fuel prices have soared since the US-Israel war with Iran began at the end of February, with the fighting severely disrupting supplies of crude oil - a key ingredient in petrol and diesel.

The rising prices have become a key issue for Americans ahead of next month's midterms elections, which will determine if Trump's Republican Party maintains control of Congress.
sources.headline: Trump faces growing backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia

stories.headline: MAGA Inc. plans late-cycle spending shifts as Republicans defend their congressional majorities

sources.body: MAGA Inc. is planning to trim the map in a homestretch bid to cling to power in November. The President Donald Trump-aligned super PAC, with several hundred million dollars still in the bank, is planning a series of major money moves coordinated with other leading GOP super PACs in the final three weeks before Election Day. The push includes cutting off spending to a group of less attainable House races, piling in money to shore up others and training its focus on key Senate seats to salvage Republicans’ Senate majority. Ohio, Alaska and Iowa are the Senate races that Trump officials view as increasingly critical to keep their majority in the chamber, according to three GOP officials familiar with MAGA Inc.’s strategy, granted anonymity to candidly assess the midterms. One of the people said MAGA Inc. and a leading House GOP super PAC would pull spending out of Michigan’s 8th District by the middle of this week. The move effectively acknowledges Democratic Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet’s strength over GOP challenger Tom Smith. They have similar plans for a group of other House races in the coming days that are trending away from Republicans. The official stressed the tacking would amount to “re-allocating, not cutting” the total planned spend. MAGA Inc. and its affiliates are still competing in all of the Senate battlegrounds, including Texas, where they expected to add at least $5 million and potentially more in the coming days, according to the official. For the Senate, winning two out of those three states of Ohio, Alaska and Iowa would make it “hard” for Democrats to take the Senate, one of the senior GOP officials projected, adding that a three-state sweep would decisively put it out of reach for Democrats. That, however, would require Republicans to win Texas and a handful of other at-risk red states, while also flipping Michigan or another blue state. The same senior Republican official said there’s confidence GOP Rep. Ashley Hinson “probably pulls through” in the Iowa Senate race. Texas, however, remains a massive headache for Republicans — and the GOP official is pointing to Ken Paxton as the problem. The senior Republican official said MAGA Inc. would do what it can to help candidates and vowed to “unload the tank” — a promise the group has been making for months even as it’s only spent more than half of the half-a-billion-dollar war chest with three weeks to go. But the onus for standing up a winning campaign is shifting. Ultimately, the official said, “it's up to the candidates, not the outside groups” to “bring it home and have a reason to get a few more points of swing voters their way.” They also need to maximize their votes with Republicans, this person said. “Over the next week to 10 days you will see a lot of moves — a lot of coordinated moves — that are around trimming the map for the home stretch,” the senior GOP official familiar with MAGA Inc.’s plans said. “It'll be all over the place. It'll just just be moving on from districts that we don't think it's the right time for, and piling in further on ones we think it is the right time for.” That would force top House GOP groups to decide whether to shift their own cash to take over key spending from MAGA Inc. as they work to defend a host of once-safely red House seats Trump won by more than 10 points in 2024 that are now at risk. That includes key districts across the Midwest, North Carolina, Nevada, along with a seat in Kentucky, which Trump won by 15 points. In Ohio, where Trump is traveling for a rally on Monday, Republicans have privately worried about GOP Sen. Jon Husted for months. The former lieutenant governor, who was appointed to serve out Vice President JD Vance’s Senate term, has been trailing former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown in public and private polling for months. The top Senate GOP super PAC, Senate Leadership Fund, has unloaded close to $100 million in Ohio and a slew of outside groups have joined, making it one of the most expensive Senate contests in the country. Just in the last week, Husted notched his first narrow lead over Brown in one recent poll . “We want a maximum spend,” Ohio GOP Chair Alex Triantafilou, who played host to Vance on Friday in Lima and will reprise that role as the president lands in Youngstown, said in an interview. “We want as much attention. I mean, the president's coming, the vice president. Look, I'm the chair of the Republican Party — I want full resources in this state. We welcome it very much.” And while Texas has emerged as an unexpectedly expensive headache for Republicans, another GOP operative familiar with MAGA Inc.'s thinking suggested Ohio could end up costing Republicans more spending from all sides, despite its smaller size. Democrats see the same final battlefield taking shape. Senate Majority PAC, the top Democratic-aliied PAC, is injecting $2.5 million in Iowa and $7 million in Ohio for television ads, according to plans shared first with POLITICO, “injecting new resources to help close the gap in those battleground states,” a spokesperson said. They’ll also continue to back aggressive digital campaigns in each state. This comes on the heels of SMP dropping $5 million in Kansas . Beyond Ohio, other senior Republicans are busy trying to staunch the bleeding in red states across the map. Top Senate GOP groups have already cut off spending in North Carolina, where Republicans are struggling to defend a GOP-held seat. They have also pulled some money back in Georgia but are still planning to unload millions more in the Peach State. Senate Leadership Fund expects to keep spending broadly across the map in the final weeks. The group plans to pour even more money into Texas as a potential lifeline to Paxton, hitting a total of nearly $200 million. They’re also dropping dough in Kansas to defend Sen. Roger Marshall, whose tough race against Democrat Adam Hamilton blindsided top Republicans in the final weeks, along with a crop of other endangered GOP incumbents, according to two Republicans with direct knowledge of the plans. And, SLF is expected to keep unloading money into the Michigan Senate race, which Senate Republicans view as their top flip opportunity. The senior GOP official familiar with MAGA Inc.’s strategy defended the group’s spending decisions, despite waves of criticism from some Republicans who wanted it to unleash all its $400-million-plus war chest, and sooner. So far, MAGA Inc. and its affiliates have spent just over $200 million this cycle, including future ad reservations, according to data from AdImpact. The cash the wider MAGA Inc. operation deployed last month, which was close to $100 million, shielded candidates from further losses as the environment worsened for Republicans, the official argued. “The money's working,” the official said. “The money stopped everybody from getting killed in September when the environment rapidly deteriorated further. The money held the line.” The campaigns that received the September spending were able to “stay afloat,” one of the other officials said. “There are more candidates in a position that they can still win their race today that wouldn't have been had that not happened.” Many of those GOP candidates, however, privately argue it was Trump’s poor approval rating and his decisions around the ongoing war with Iran, tariffs and sky-high fuel prices that are sparking voter backlash. It was during that September panic that GOP officials became increasingly worried about the growing map. At one point, Trump officials believed they may need to start intervening to boost even Sen. Ashley Moody in ruby-red Florida as warning signs shot up across the Sunshine State, according to two Trump officials with direct knowledge of the matter. But recent internal polling for Moody has turned a corner, alleviating many of those concerns and prompting Trump officials to stand by plans for the president to visit the state — but more as a way to boost Rep. Byron Donalds, who is running for governor, and several key House races that Republicans are worried about, according to the people. Jessica Piper contributed to this report.
sources.headline: MAGA Inc. plots final midterm money moves

También se produjo la intrusión de buques de guerra marroquíes en aguas de la ciudad autónoma, según han confirmado a EL PAÍS fuentes conocedoras de estos incidentes. Al menos una fragata y varias patrulleras de la Marina Real de Marruecos navegaron sin pedir autorización por aguas de soberanía española. No se trató, explican las fuentes consultadas, de un mero tránsito o de una entrada accidental, sino de una<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-09/mohamed-vi-advierte-de-que-la-cooperacion-con-espana-no-debe-verse-sometida-a-presion-amenaza-ni-chantaje.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-09/mohamed-vi-advierte-de-que-la-cooperacion-con-espana-no-debe-verse-sometida-a-presion-amenaza-ni-chantaje.html"> vulneración intencionada y repetida del mar territorial</a>, de la que hay pocos precedentes. Las incursiones navales de Marruecos se prolongaron durante los primeros días de agosto, en medio de una fuerte tensión, y estuvieron a punto de provocar una colisión entre barcos militares de los dos países. Solo después de que la Armada española desplegara buques en esas aguas y de una gestión de alto nivel por parte del Ministerio de Defensa cesó la Marina marroquí en su actitud.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-12/buques-de-guerra-marroquies-invadieron-aguas-de-ceuta-coincidiendo-con-la-entrada-masiva-de-inmigrantes.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Buques de guerra marroquíes entraron en aguas de Ceuta coincidiendo con la llegada masiva de inmigrantes

sources.body:
Buques de guerra marroquíes entraron en aguas de la ciudad autónoma de Ceuta durante la entrada de más de 70.000 migrantes en Ceuta desde Marruecos a través de la frontera del Tarajal el 30 y 31 de julio, según ha adelantado El País y ha confirmado el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, en un corrillo con periodistas en el que estaba RTVE.

La Armada envió una fragata para frenar las incursiones de la Marina de Mohamed VI en el mar bajo soberanía española.

"Tenemos que ser conscientes de que, entre dos países vecinos, esos hechos puntuales existen ", ha admitido el jefe del Ejecutivo en un corrillo con periodistas en el Palacio Real, tras la celebración del desfile de las Fuerzas Armadas con motivo del Día de la Fiesta Nacional . Un corrillo que tiene lugar, precisamente, un día antes de que los reyes viajen a Ceuta.

Con todo, Sánchez ha recalcado que tras ese hecho "hablaron las armadas" de ambos países. "Somos (países) vecinos. Fueron días intensos, pero la colaboración entre las armadas es fluida , al margen de ese hecho", ha insistido.

Sánchez ha recalcado que las relaciones con Marruecos "son muy importantes" y ha puesto en valor cuestiones como la cooperación en materias como la lucha antiterrorista o contra las mafias. "Esa relación bilateral es fundamental", ha proseguido.

También ha subrayado que eso es lo que trata de "construir" el Gobierno y no de destruir, como a su juicio, hace el PP, "que pide en la Unión Europea suspender un acuerdo estratégico" con Marruecos y que "vota contra el acuerdo de amistad con Francia".

stories.headline: Spain’s left struggles to unite its electoral alliances as ERC and Podemos strike a campaign deal

sources.body: <p>Podemos y Esquerra Republicana han hecho oficial este lunes a mediodía un acuerdo para colaborar en la campaña de las generales del 29-N. Este pacto, trasladado después de que el domingo Gabriel Rufián, actual portavoz de los republicanos en el Congreso, decidiera volver a liderar la lista <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2026-10-11/rufian-sera-candidato-por-esquerra-republicana-el-29-n.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2026-10-11/rufian-sera-candidato-por-esquerra-republicana-el-29-n.html">de su partido</a>, se concreta en dos sentidos: la formación de Ione Belarra “contribuirá a la candidatura de Esquerra Republicana” en Cataluña e Irene Montero y Gabriel Rufián “harán equipo en actos de campaña”. Es decir, la formación morada no se presentará en las cuatro demarcaciones catalanas evitando así competir contra ERC, que sopesa cederles sitios en la lista como independientes. A cambio, los dos dirigentes participarán juntos en actos por el territorio. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-12/podemos-y-erc-oficializan-el-acuerdo-por-el-que-rufian-y-montero-haran-campana-juntos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Comuns acusa a Rufián de azuzar la división en las izquierdas

sources.body:
El portavoz de ERC en el Congreso, Gabriel Rufián; la periodista Sarah Santaolalla y el diputado de Más Madrid en la Asamblea, Emilio Delgado. / César Vallejo Rodríguez / Europa Press

La cuenta atrás para presentar coaliciones marca ya menos de cinco días. Las 23.59 horas del próximo viernes se perfilan como el acantilado por el que los partidos a la izquierda del PSOE se podrían despeñar si no logran antes un acuerdo de unidad que dé vida al Frente Amplio de IU , En Comú Podem , Más Madrid y Movimiento Sumar . Sin embargo, el 'sí' de Gabriel Rufián a ERC y su pacto con Podemos han agitado unas negociaciones en las que todavía se tienen que cerrar dos cuestiones básicas: quién será el candidato y si los morados se suman a este proyecto para ir en una lista unitaria en la mayoría del país.

El portavoz de ERC en Madrid llevaba más de un año reclamando unidad a la izquierda del PSOE y apostando por buscar una fórmula que permitiera reducir a una las listas electorales en todos los territorios para maximizar los resultados. No obstante, pese a los ofrecimientos para que se sumara al Frente Amplio como candidato, Rufián cerró este domingo su candidatura por ERC , renunciando a liderar un proyecto estatal.

Lo hizo tras lograr que Esquerra cerrara un acuerdo con Podemos para incluir a un dirigente morado en las listas republicanas en Catalunya a cambio de que no se presenten en este territorio y sin formar ninguna coalición electoral. Rufián, a cambio, hará campaña por Irene Montero en el resto del Estado, aunque por el momento se desconoce si la candidata de Podemos se presentará en solitario o terminará buscando una alianza con el Frente Amplio.

El pacto ERC-Podemos ha enervado a los Comuns, quienes, en un comunicado, han remarcado "la profunda decepción" que sienten por el dirigente de Esquerra porque "venía a unificar a las izquierdas y está haciendo todo lo posible por dividirlas". El partido mantiene que su apuesta es el Frente Amplio y que su candidata a liderarlo es la exalcaldesa de Barcelona, Ada Colau.

El portavoz de ERC en el Congreso, Gabriel Rufián / Fernando Sánchez - Europa Press

Los partidos del antiguo Sumar llevan desde febrero, cuando Yolanda Díaz anunció su paso atrás, dedicados a buscar a un nuevo candidato. Sin embargo, a menos de 50 días de las elecciones, siguen sin tenerlo. En los últimos meses se pusieron sobre la mesa los nombres de Pablo Bustinduy , ministro de Derechos Sociales; Ernest Urtasun , responsable de Cultura; e, incluso, de Unai Sordo , líder de CCOO. Y solo en la última semana se plantearon las opciones de Mónica García , líder de Más Madrid y ministra de Sanidad; Ada Colau , exalcaldesa de Barcelona; y del propio Rufián.

La decisión de Rufián ha dejado al Frente Amplio sin una de las bazas que, durante unos pocos días, fue la mejor apuesta que tenían. Ahora, Más Madrid plantea como cabeza de lista por Madrid a Emilio Delgado , dirigente autonómico que compartió un acto con Rufián. Sin embargo, Izquierda Unida sigue apostando por Ada Colau, a quien había propuesto precisamente Más Madrid. Y en un intento por rebajar tensiones, la portavoz de Movimiento Sumar, Verónica Barbero , plantea la opción de un tándem entre ambos.
sources.headline: La izquierda, en el laberinto de los pactos: ¿Quién liderará Frente Amplio? ¿Qué ha acordado ERC con Podemos?

stories.headline: US Navy’s sixth guided-missile destroyer is due to arrive at the Rota naval base

sources.body: <p>En pleno repliegue de las tropas estadounidenses en Europa, Washington refuerza su presencia militar en España. El próximo jueves llegará a Rota (Cádiz) el <i>USS John Basilone,</i> el sexto destructor lanzamisiles de la Navy desplegado en la base naval gaditana. Se completará así la ampliación con dos nuevos buques de la Fuerzas Navales de Despliegue Avanzado en Europa (FDND-E), acordada por el presidente español, Pedro Sánchez, y el estadounidense Joe Biden en la cumbre de la OTAN celebrada en Madrid en 2022. Está previsto que acudan a Rota para recibir al buque la ministra de Defensa, Margarita Robles, el embajador de Estados Unidos en Madrid, Benjamin LeónJ r, y el comandante de la Sexta Flota, el vicealmirante Jeffrey T. Anderson, con base en Nápoles.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-12/el-sexto-destructor-lanzamisiles-de-ee-uu-llegara-este-jueves-a-la-base-naval-de-rota.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El sexto destructor lanzamisiles de EE UU llegará este jueves a la base naval de Rota

stories.headline: Spain’s Constitutional Court ruling on the amnesty law could clear the way for Carles Puigdemont’s return

sources.body: <p>Cándido Conde-Pumpido (A Coruña, 77 años), presidente del Tribunal Constitucional, ha elaborado la sentencia que pone fin al debate jurídico sobre la aplicación de la ley de amnistía a los líderes del <i>procés</i>. La resolución, aprobada esta semana, cuestiona la interpretación de la norma que hizo el Tribunal Supremo, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/via-libre-al-regreso-de-puigdemont-el-constitucional-ordena-al-supremo-que-amnistie-la-malversacion-del-proces.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/via-libre-al-regreso-de-puigdemont-el-constitucional-ordena-al-supremo-que-amnistie-la-malversacion-del-proces.html">ordena al alto tribunal que aplique el perdón también al delito de malversación</a> y fija la doctrina constitucional sobre el asunto. La decisión, de trascendencia histórica, abre la puerta a que el <i>expresident</i> Carles Puigdemont pueda regresar a España nueve años después de huir tras el proceso independentista que provocó una profunda fractura política y social en Cataluña y que planteó uno de los mayores desafíos constitucionales a los que se ha enfrentado España desde la Transición.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-11/candido-conde-pumpido-cuestionar-al-tribunal-constitucional-es-cuestionar-la-democracia.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/UOK2E4CS7VESXLL3OHJUP6SHBE.jpg?auth=48601a3f3eafd12c7ed6705182f285080fd92e7035413cfba7a20dea83f6cb03" width="8192" height="5464" alt="Cándido Conde-Pumpido, durante la entrevista este viernes en la sede del Constitucional en Madrid"></img>
sources.headline: Cándido Conde-Pumpido: “Cuestionar al Tribunal Constitucional es cuestionar la democracia”

stories.headline: Housing encampment and competing demonstrations shape Barcelona’s October 12 holiday

sources.body: El 12 d’octubre a Barcelona està condicionat aquest anys per la proximitat de les eleccions generals i la crisi de l’habitatge , escenificada per l’acampada a la plaça de Catalunya. I com cada any, es convoquen diverses manifestacions de caire contrari . D’una banda, diverses entitats unionistes han organitzat una manifestació que recorre el passeig de Gràcia a partir del migdia per commemorar el Dia de la Hispanitat . La mobilització porta el lema “Catalunya amb Ceuta. Una mateixa Espanya” per situar la ciutat autònoma en el centre de la celebració. També et pot interessar Manifestacions el 12 d’octubre a Barcelona pel Dia de la Hispanitat 2026: què s’ha convocat? Eva Vial 3 minuts de lectura De l’altra, col·lectius antifeixistes i antiracistes han convocat protestes al carrer per mostrar el rebuig a aquesta data. La plataforma Som Antifeixistes ha convocat aquest matí una manifestació a Nou Barris sota el lema “Imperi espanyol, racista i genocida”. A la tarda, el Bloc Anticolonial ha organitzat una mobilització antiracista, que arrencarà a les 18 h des de la seu de la Direcció General de Prevenció i Protecció de la Infància i l’Adolescència, a l’avinguda del Paral·lel, 53. El lema és “Davant del colonialisme, memòria, ràbia i dignitat migrant. Al genocidi, ni oblit ni perdó ni ara ni al 1492”. En aquesta pàgina pots seguir minut a minut totes les incidències que passin en aquest 12-O.
sources.headline: 2.000 persones es manifesten en un 12-O marcat per l’habitatge i les eleccions | DIRECTE

sources.body:
Jóvenes de ultraderecha increpan a los acampados en la Puerta del Sol. / Eduardo Parra / Europa Press

Las acampadas en la madrileña Puerta del Sol y en la plaza de Catalunya de Barcelona (y otras ciudades españolas) se mantienen como protesta por la crisis de la vivienda . El Gobierno decidió convocar elecciones el próximo 29 de noviembre tras la oposición de Junts a las medidas del Gobierno para regular la vivienda. La muerte de Maricarmen, la octogenaria desahuciada en Madrid que originó las protestas, reactiva la vivienda como eje de la próxima campaña electoral y de cara a la huelga general del 11N .

EL PERIÓDICO abre un hilo directo con las últimas noticias sobre la acampada en Sol, las protestas por los alquileres y las leyes sobre la vivienda.

Agentes de Policía Nacional están incrementando la presión en la céntrica plaza de la Puerta del Sol para separar a los concentrados de la acampada por la vivienda de jóvenes de ultraderecha. Han elaborado un cordón entre ambos bandos y han pedido refuerzos para controlar la situación. Los efectivos desplazado a los recién llegados a las bocacalles de Espoz y Mina y de la Carrera de San Jerónimo, que desemboca en el cercano Paseo del Prado, donde se ha celebrado el desfile militar por el 12 de octubre del que podrían haber llegado parte de los congregados. Se escuchan proclamas contra el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, 'rojo el que no bote', 'a por ellos' y algunos individuos han realizado saludo fascista con el brazo en alto. También han arrojado huevos a los acampados y les han enseñado jabón. Desde los manifestantes de Sol se ha coreado 'Aquí están los antifascistas' y 'chicos, recordad que mañana hay cole', en alusión a la juventud de muchos de los provocadores.

Jóvenes de ultraderecha ante la Policía en la Puerta del Sol. / EP

Efectivos de Policía Nacional se han desplegado en la céntrica plaza de la Puerta del Sol para separar a grupos de jóvenes de ultraderecha de los concentrados en la acampada por la vivienda. La Policía ha establecido un cordón alrededor del campamento, y los manifestantes que han acudido en parte del desfile militar por el 12 de octubre increpan a los acampados. Desde los manifestantes de Sol se ha coreado 'Aquí están los antifascistas', mientras que desde el lado contrario se han escuchado proclamas contra el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, 'rojo el que no bote' y han realizado saludo fascista con el brazo en alto y con banderas preconstitucionales. Se trata en su mayoría de jóvenes, incluso menores de edad con actitudes provocadoras. La Policía no ha realizado por el momento maniobras para ahuyentar a los congregados.

Jóvenes de ultraderecha en la Puerta del Sol. / EP

Grupos de jóvenes de ultraderecha increpan en estos momentos a los acampados en la Puerta del Sol en defensa de la vivienda digna. La policía se mantiene ante los concentrados pero sin actuar.

Jóvenes de ultraderecha intentan desestabilizar la acampada de la Puerta del Sol. / 24H

Momentos de tensión en la acampada de la plaza del Sol de Madrid por la presencia de personas que se han acercado tras asistir al desfile militar y que son contrarios a la acampada.
sources.headline: Directo | Tensión en la Puerta del Sol al acudir a la acampada asistentes en el desfile del 12-O

stories.headline: Mossos investigate fatal stabbing after a group attack in Barcelona’s Nou Barris district

sources.body: (ACN) Els Mossos d’Esquadra investiguen la mort violenta d’un home aquesta matinada al barri de les Roquetes , al districte de Nou Barris. La policia catalana ha rebut un avís cap a les 2 h d’aquest dilluns per una agressió comesa per un grup de persones, possiblement amb arma blanca, contra un home al carrer de Romaní. Quan han arribat al lloc dels fets, els agents han localitzat una persona ferida que posteriorment ha mort. A més dels Mossos, el Sistema d’Emergències Mèdiques (SEM) hi ha desplaçat quatre ambulàncies. Tot i les maniobres de reanimació practicades inicialment pels mossos i pels efectius del SEM, la víctima ha acabat morint. La Divisió d’Investigació Criminal (DIC) de Barcelona ha obert una investigació per esclarir les circumstàncies dels fets. La investigació resta sota secret de les actuacions. També et pot interessar Un detingut per la mort violenta d’un home a Nou Barris Redacció 1 minut de lectura
sources.headline: Els Mossos investiguen la mort d’un home per arma blanca aquesta matinada a les Roquetes

stories.headline: Barcelona’s TMB bus workers announce seven strike days in October over a demand for a 35-hour workweek

sources.body:
La plantilla de busos de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona ( TMB ) està en vaga per reclamar millores laborals. Les dues reivindicacions principals són jornades setmanals de 35 hores i fer dos festius consecutius. Per exigir el compliment de les demandes, els treballadors han convocat set dies d’aturades parcials aquest octubre. El primer va ser aquest dijous, 8 d’octubre. La resta de dies de vaga seran el 14, 15, 20, 22, 27 i 29.

El secretari general de la Confederació General de Treballadors ( CGT ) de bus a TMB, Óscar Mellado, ha explicat que actualment tenen un horari d’unes 37,5 hores setmanals. El plantejament que fan és que es pugui reduir a les 35 hores, com s’aplica a algunes administracions públiques, com l’Ajuntament de Barcelona, després de l’aprovació del conveni laboral municipal. El seu company al sindicat, Jordi Ballesté, ha recordat que la reivindicació dels dos dies festius consecutius està avalada des de fa dos anys per la justícia, però no s’està aplicant.

🚌⚠️ Avui, dijous 8 d’octubre, afectacions al servei de #busbcn per convocatòria de vaga. ⏰ Franges afectades: 🔹De 9 a 11 h. 🔹De 19 a 21 h. 🔹De 23 h i fins a la finalització del servei. ✅ Serveis mínims: 🔹40% en hores punta. 🔹20% en hores vall. ℹ️ Més informació a https://t.co/6FFKkqkDoO i a través d’aquest canal.

Mellado ha dit al TOT Barcelona que la vaga de dijous va tenir un seguiment molt ampli. “Vaig estar a la cotxera d’Horta al matí i era de quasi el 100%”. En canvi, des de l’empresa metropolitana de transport van xifrar l’aturada en un 66%.

Fa anys que els conductors de bus de TMB opten per aturades parcials. Aquest octubre, els busos funcionaran amb serveis mínims els dies 14, 15, 20, 22, 27 i 29. Les franges horàries afectades són entre les 09.00 i 11.00 del matí; entre les 19.00 i 21.00 hores, i des de les 23.00 hores fins a la finalització del servei. La Generalitat va decretar uns serveis mínims que oscil·len entre el 20 i 40%, aquest darrer percentatge en hora punta.

La plantilla de bus de @TMB_Barcelona @TMBinfo decideix anar a la vaga després de 23 reunions i 4 mediacions pel nou conveni col·lectiu @laiabonetrull VOL EL CONFLICTE I L’HA ACONSEGUIT @CGTCatalunya @CGTBarcelona @CGTmetroBCN https://t.co/qiHG0UILh2

Sense concretar què han ofert a la plantilla, fonts de TMB han subratllat que la direcció lamenta que els sindicats hagin rebutjat la darrera proposta i confia que tornin a la taula de negociació per tal d’arribar a un acord com més aviat millor.

La plantilla de busos va decidir anar a la vaga després de celebrar una assemblea massiva -amb aturada del servei- el 22 de setembre. Mellado ha concretat que des del novembre passat han fet vint-i-tres reunions amb la direcció de TMB i cinc reunions de mediació al departament de Treball.
sources.headline: Set dies de vaga als busos de TMB a l’octubre: la plantilla reclama les 35 hores setmanals
